reply: I added problem 6 (Andre's equation) after problem 5, with the error located in the step where the x terms are combined and the solution x = -1, worth 2 points.

problem.text: Andre solved an equation, but when he checked his answer he saw his solution was incorrect. He knows he made a mistake, but he can't find it. Where is Andre's mistake and what is the solution to the equation? \(-2(3x-5)=4(x+3)+8\); work shown: \(-6x+10=4x+12+8\); \(-6x+10=4x+20\); \(10=-2x+20\); \(-10=-2x\); \(5=x\)
problem.answerKey: Mistake: in the step from -6x + 10 = 4x + 20 to 10 = -2x + 20, Andre combined 4x and -6x as -2x, which moves -6x to the right side with the wrong sign. Adding 6x to both sides gives 10 = 10x + 20. Correct solution: 10x = -10, so x = -1. Check: LHS -2(3(-1) - 5) = 16 and RHS 4(-1 + 3) + 8 = 16.
problem.gradingNotes: Accept -1 in any equivalent form. Students may name the error in different words, but it must point to the step where the x terms were moved. Each point is independent of the other.

rubric.description: 1 pt: identifies the mistake in the step from -6x + 10 = 4x + 20 to 10 = -2x + 20, where -6x was moved with the wrong sign (should give 10 = 10x + 20)
1 pt: correct solution x = -1
